Run the detector on candidate 1 of the source of each of the ten main scenes (SA01 to SA10) with two kinds of query. Present: the scene's rearrangement-object queries (19 in all; SA06 has one query, 'an oar'). Absent: eight objects that cannot appear in a scene plausible for 1900 to 1925 (a smartphone; a laptop computer; a television set; a computer keyboard; a plastic water bottle; a jet airplane; a satellite dish; a microwave oven), the same eight for every scene (80 in all). Each query's score is its best box's score. Every observed score is a possible cut c; Youden's J(c) is the share of present scores at or above c minus the share of absent scores at or above c. c* is the smallest observed score with the largest J. The score cut is the midpoint between c* and the largest observed score below c*, rounded to three decimals. A detection counts when its score is at least the cut.
Two boxes for one query are the same object when their IoU is at least 0.5 (fixed, not set from data).
Per-pixel difference d: the Euclidean distance between the two images' RGB values (0 to 441), with no smoothing.

Over every pixel of candidate 1 of the small and of the medium addition of each of the ten main scenes (20 raw edits, each compared with the source it was made from), take the median m and the median absolute deviation MAD of d. The threshold is m + 3.5 x MAD / 0.6745, the value at which a pixel's modified z-score (Iglewicz and Hoaglin, 1993) passes 3.5, rounded to one decimal. A pixel is marked as changed when d is above the threshold.

With that threshold, find every 8-connected group of marked pixels in the same 20 edits. The speck size is the 99.9th percentile of the groups' sizes in pixels, rounded up to a whole number. Every group of at most that many pixels is a speck and is removed; then every unmarked area wholly enclosed by marked pixels is filled. The result is the cleaned change mask.

With the cleaned change masks of the same 20 edits, for each whole-pixel distance k = 1, 2, ... from the mask (Euclidean distance), take the median of d over the pixels whose distance lies in (k - 1, k], pooled over the 20 edits. The widening radius is the smallest k whose ring median is at most m, the median of d over all pixels (the level of the model's re-rendering of an unchanged pixel), so the edge of the pasted region falls where the edit differs from its input no more than a typical pixel does. If no k up to 64 qualifies, the radius is 64.
Every pixel within the widening radius of the cleaned mask (Euclidean distance), with enclosed holes filled.

The accepted file takes the raw edit's pixels inside the widened mask and the input's pixels everywhere else (input = the accepted source for small and medium; the accepted, composited medium file for large).

Share of the image (percent of 1536 x 1024 pixels) inside the cleaned change mask of the composited file compared with the accepted source, computed with the same threshold and cleaning. For the large file this includes the medium element.
